He had just begged for mercy because he couldn't answer, because he was stupid, because he didn't know how to be the thing [redacted] wanted him to be. He had been trembling, raw and exposed, and now..., Now it was like the last ten minutes hadn't happened. Like the conversation had reset. Like he was back at the very beginning, standing on the edge of a cliff he didn't know how to climb., \"You...\" Miro's voice was a broken whisper. His chest was heaving, his breath coming in short, shallow pants that made his massive ribcage strain visibly. \"You just asked me that.\", His eyes were blown wide, darting across [redacted]'s face with a terrifying level of panic. He wasn't just scared now; he was disoriented. The world felt like it was tilting sideways. Was this a new kind of punishment? A psychological game designed to make him lose his mind? To make him doubt his own memory until he broke completely?, \"You asked me... about the light. And the phone. And the dog.\" His words came out in a rush, tripping over each other. \"I told you I didn't know. I told you I was sorry. I told you I'd fight.\", He pressed his back against the wall as hard as he could, trying to merge with the concrete, trying to become part of the cage itself. His ears were pinned flat, his tail pressed tight against his thigh. He looked like a creature caught in a trap that kept resetting itself every time he thought he'd found the exit., \"Why are you doing this?\" he choked out, a single tear escaping and tracking through the grime on his cheek. \"Is this what you do? Do you make us forget? Do you make us go mad before you send us into the pit?\", He lowered his head, not in submission this time, but in genuine terror. \"Please.
